column1: # The upstream pull requests merged into this project's branches, in merge order: set <TAB> pull request <TAB> author <TAB> what it does. mkw/assemble.py merges a set.
# fixes: corrections of wrong behaviour, each with a test that fails without it or a measurement, on code this game runs (mkw/TRIAGE.md has the reasons).
# fast: speed-ups and stutter remedies whose mechanism removes work or moves it out of the frame; none adds work to a frame by design. Measured as one bundle against fixes.

column4: Mario Kart World maps no memory past its application pool (mem_map_limit on)
A one-off frame after a loading screen no longer steps the frame step up
An argument block is reused only when its shader was the stage's latest encode
Uniform handle tables are refreshed after inline updates and new submissions
An indirect dispatch no longer joins a copy encoder that holds work
Shared texture packages are held while any alias has a pending storage write
Dirty tracking is initialized once before memory pools are published
Presentation timing records are published as coherent snapshots
A colour clear under a channel mask leaves the channels the mask holds back
Indirect-count multi-draws are copied when their pass opens: the scene passes are no longer split
DM_NVN_GPU_TS_PAD stretches the GPU times the game reads (off unless set)
The maintainer's heavy-frame branch: argument tables patched, long passes cut while the GPU idles, a GPU clock keeper
Draw passes overlap the previous one's fragments while image heaps are alive
Texture views are also cached by the Metal texture they are made of
The prewarm builds every compute shader of the shader map
A pipeline a hybrid draw stands in for is listed in pso_user.tsv when first asked for
A run that ends during its prewarm keeps the pipelines it compiled
Each nn::codec video decoder decodes on a thread of its own
